cards.text: Now we meet a man named Micah (not the prophet Micah) from the hill country of Ephraim. Somebody took eleven hundred shekels of silver from his mother, and Micah heard her utter a curse about it. Now Micah has something to tell her.

cards.question: Micah's mother lost eleven hundred shekels of silver and uttered a curse about it. True or false: Micah tells her he's the one who took it.
Micah just admitted he took his mother's eleven hundred shekels. What does she say?

answers.text: Blessed be my son by the LORD
Shame on my son before the LORD
My son has brought a curse on us

cards.question: Micah gives the eleven hundred shekels back, and his mother says she wholly dedicates the silver to the LORD for her son's benefit. What does she want it made into?

answers.text: A graven image and a molten idol
A gold lampstand for the tabernacle

cards.text: She says she'll return the silver to Micah, and he returns it to her, so that silver's been passed back and forth more than the last cookie on the plate. Then she gives two hundred shekels to a silversmith, who makes the graven image and the molten idol.

cards.question: Once the silversmith makes the graven image and the molten idol, they are placed in Micah's ___.

cards.text: Micah has a shrine too, and he makes an ephod and some household idols. This man's got more gear than I've got sprinkles, and I've got a LOT of sprinkles.

cards.question: Micah has a shrine, an ephod and household idols. To be his priest, he ordains one of his ___.

cards.text: Then the writer steps back from Micah's house and says something about the whole country: "In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes."

cards.question: In those days, with no king in Israel, who decides what is right for each person?

answers.text: The elders decide for each town

cards.text: Now somebody new walks into the story: a young Levite, from the tribe set apart to serve at God's tabernacle (Numbers 3:6-7), who comes from Bethlehem in Judah and has been living within the clan of Judah. Then he picks up and leaves Bethlehem.

cards.question: True or false: the young Levite leaves Bethlehem in Judah because Micah sent for him.

cards.text: His travels bring him to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim, and Micah asks where he's from. He says he's a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I bet Micah's ears perk up like mine do when the oven timer dings.

cards.question: Micah asks the young Levite to stay and be his father and priest. What does Micah offer him in return?

answers.text: Ten shekels a year plus clothes and provisions
Two hundred shekels and a house of his own
A field and a share of the flocks

cards.text: The Levite goes in and agrees to stay. I spent years in a junk drawer, and the best offer I ever got was a rubber band asking if I wanted to stretch.

cards.question: Micah asked the young Levite to be his father and priest. The young man stays, and he becomes like a ___ to Micah.
True or false: Micah ordains the young Levite, and he becomes Micah's priest and lives in Micah's house.
Micah says, "Now I know that the LORD will be good to me…" Why is Micah so sure?

answers.text: Because a Levite has become his priest
Because his mother blessed him by the LORD
Because the silver went back to his mother

cards.text: Micah's sure he's got everything figured out. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is still in the oven.
